messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTOMATED ALERT — streaming-payload-stutter detected. p95 >= 1.2s, p99 >= 3s over the last 5m. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate/stream, /v1/chat/stream. Paging #incidents to on-call. Thread TS: 4776543210

alice: acked — I'm on call. triaging now.

alice: quick note: spike started ~4776543185 and coincides with small jump in connection resets from streaming-proxy. metrics: streaming-proxy write latency p95 900ms -> 1.4s, queue depth up x3.

bob: adding context from runtime side — we rolled model-variant canary yesterday that increases tokenization overhead for short responses. could be contributing but the proxy-level stalls suggest buffering/backpressure.

carla: I'm pulling traces. initial correlation shows long gaps between chunks (clients reporting long pauses mid-stream). downstream TCP stats show many connections with stalled send window.

elaine: support: three customers (acct-237, acct-891, acct-1902) reported timeouts and truncated streams. severity: degraded UX, some 502s seen by customers. I've opened tickets and sent preliminary status.

dmitri: flagged customer impact — prioritizing mitigation. Do we know if this affects hosted Dedicated customers differently?

alice: good question — from quick shot, Dedicated instances on customers' own pools not impacted. This seems concentrated in the public streaming-router cluster (eu-west-1 and us-east-1).

frank: /svc/streaming-proxy pods in eu-west-1 show high go-routines waiting on write. kernel socket buffers are filling then timing out. seen ERR: "write: connection timed out" in proxy logs.

bob: hypothesis: intermittent client backpressure + proxy chunk aggregation leads to head-of-line stalls. proxy's chunking_wait_ms might be too aggressive under these conditions.

alice: can we try an immediate mitigation: reduce chunking_wait_ms and increase proxy keepalive/write timeout? low-risk config flip.

frank: I can flip on a conservative change in eu-west-1 1) chunking_wait_ms 1200 -> 400, 2) proxy_write_timeout 25s -> 45s. rolling restart of proxy pool to pick up config. doing a small canary (2 pods) first.

carla: logs during replication: examples of stalled chunk sequence:
```
[2026-03-15T12:07:02Z] client_conn=abcd stream_id=987 chunk_id=5 state=waiting_for_buffered_write
[2026-03-15T12:07:08Z] client_conn=abcd stream_id=987 chunk_id=5 write_error=timeout
```
shows 6s pause then timeout.

frank: canary applied to 2 pods at 12:09Z. will monitor.

bob: also propose temporarily routing traffic away from older proxy instances with known slow syscall latencies (node group pg-stream-legacy). scaling up newer pool helps.

alice: scaling new pool + canary config — do it. frank, can you kick off scale now?

frank: scaling new pool +3 pods in us-east and eu-west now.

elaine: telling affected customers we are investigating and applying mitigations; ETA 15-30m to see impact.

carla: realtime metrics after canary: eu-west chunk gap p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~0.5s on canary pods. overall p95 trending down.

incident-bot: NOTE: engagement window — paging still active. please update this thread with mitigation steps and customer notifications.

alice: observed partial mitigation — p95 back to ~650ms cluster-wide, p99 still ~1.9s. some customers still seeing intermittent truncation.

bob: chasing logs on ingress LB — saw occasional large TCP retransmit bursts from a small subset of client IPs (likely heavy clients). could be slow consumer problem. adding short-term per-connection rate cap to limit head-of-line impact.

frank: applied connection-rate cap at LB layer for top offending IPs. also reduced chunk-size threshold for proxy (now 32KB -> 16KB) on canary.

carla: after rate-caps + chunk-size tweak metrics: p99 improved from 1.9s -> 1.1s in eu-west, overall error rate down 70%.

elaine: customers updated: two confirmed improvement, one still reporting issues (acct-1902). support escalated to account ops.

dmitri: acct-1902 is on a custom integration; ask for trace id and sample logs. Elaine, please request request-id from them.

elaine: asked for request-id; they provided id=req_0a7fcb. attached to support ticket #INC-1902.

alice: looking at req_0a7fcb — shows server-side chunk pause at 12:06:58Z lasting ~12s then a keepalive-triggered retry. that instance was on an older kernel version (pg-stream-legacy).

bob: action item: decommission legacy node group for streaming-router — schedule after immediate mitigation. For now, we've shifted customer sessions away.

frank: rolling restart of legacy nodes to drain sessions. also increasing streaming-proxy pool to handle backlog (temporary +20% capacity).

carla: adding observability items: set up a short-term anomaly alert for chunk gap p95 > 1s and socket retransmit > 100/s per node.

incident-bot: UPDATE: mitigation in progress — canary config ok, scaling applied, customer notifications sent.

alice: status update for handoff: immediate mitigation appears effective. p95 back to acceptable ranges (~400-700ms), p99 ~900-1100ms. no new customer escalations in last 10m.

alice: handing off to bob/runtime for root cause + postmortem. Bob, please pick up deeper analysis (kernel-level socket handling + chunking heuristic). I will remain available for followups.

bob: ack — I'll own RCA. immediate next steps: collect tcpdump from affected legacy nodes, gather proxy write syscall histograms, review canary config diff. scheduling postmortem slot tomorrow 09:30 UTC.

elaine: sending final customer update: "We've applied mitigations and performance is improving; root cause investigation ongoing. We'll follow up with postmortem." :thumbsup:

dmitri: thanks team. please add timeline and customer impact summary to the incident doc.

frank: one-liner mitigation summary I added to config-change log: "temporary chunking_wait_ms reduction, chunk_size threshold lowered, keepalive increased, per-connection rate caps applied, scaled proxy pool."

carla: logging note: saved trace ids and sample latency traces to /incidents/4776543210/artifacts for postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. owner: bob (eng-runtime). followup: RCA + postmortem assigned. severity: P2 (customer-impacting but mitigated).

alice: closing live-handoff. if conditions regress, re-page urgent. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
